subject: Learning Methods
title: What to Capture and What to Skip
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on What to Capture and What to Skip.

hook.text: He wrote down everything the professor said. His notes were 20 pages long. He could not find the key ideas afterward.

buildup.text: Effective note-taking requires selection. Not everything is worth recording. The skill is in deciding what matters.

discovery.text: Capture main ideas, supporting evidence, and anything that surprises you. Skip repetition, filler, and obvious context.

twist.text: The fear of missing something drives over-capturing. But too many notes dilute the important points in a sea of noise.

climax.text: Aim for the 20% that carries 80% of the meaning. If you can't identify the core, you don't yet understand the material.

punchline.text: Less is more. Capture only what matters most.

quiz.question: Why is over-capturing harmful to note quality?
options: It uses too much paper or storage
Important points get buried in a sea of less important details
It makes handwriting worse due to speed
